thread:
janet: Customer acct acme-inc reporting repeated 503s from hosted API starting ~10:42 UTC. They see timeouts and gateway errors. Raising to infra. :rotating_light:

matt: Thanks — any request IDs or sample traces?

janet: sample request id 7c9f3a, route /v1/generate, model=rwd-13b. Attached short excerpt from our gateway logs: 

```
2026-03-17T10:42:13Z gateway: upstream 10.4.32.11:8080 returned 503 for req=7c9f3a
2026-03-17T10:42:13Z gateway: connection reset by peer
2026-03-17T10:42:14Z proxy: error reading response: EOF
```

matt: grabbing runner logs now. Seen similar transient 503s on other clusters — will post findings.

matt: quick grep from runner pod infer-runner-84c9: 

```
[2026-03-17T10:41:59Z] infer-runner[pid=2145]: ERROR: upstream process exited with signal 15 (SIGTERM)
[2026-03-17T10:42:01Z] infer-runner[pid=2145]: backtrace saved to /var/crash/core.2145
[2026-03-17T10:42:02Z] nvml: NVRM: Xid (13) - a GPU page fault or driver stop
[2026-03-17T10:42:02Z] model-infer: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. attempted allocate 1.2GiB
```

matt: pattern is SIGTERM then coredump then immediate restart. Could be our watchdog killing after OOM or kernel driver forcing reset.

sara: :eyes: Which model variant? rwd-13b default uses 8-bit quant on A100? If process tried to allocate large tensor, could be kv-prefetch/batch config regression. Any recent rollout?

matt: No recent model change on that pool. We did push a batch/prefetch heuristic tweak yesterday (eng-runtime) — rolling back to confirm.

ryan: Repro plan: can we trigger locally with scaled qps script? If it's OOM then we should reproduce by sending long context + high batch concurrency. I'll spin up a dev runner with verbose mem logging.

janet: Customer impact: ~15% of requests for acme-inc in us-west-2 failed with 503 between 10:42–10:49. They hit a retry loop and saw increased latency. Escalation call scheduled in 30m.

matt: Temporary mitigations I can apply now: 1) route acme-inc traffic to fallback pool (smaller model/quantized) 2) disable prefetch on affected pool 3) mark pool as drain for new jobs to avoid cascading restarts. Which do we want?

sara: Do 1 + 2. Fallback to rwd-7b-quant should preserve client experience. Also collect core and nvcrash logs to S3: `aws s3 cp /var/crash/core.2145 s3://redwood-debug/acme/2754321987/`

matt: Doing it now. Running: `kubectl annotate svc acme-inc-route reroute=fallback-7b-quant --overwrite` and `kubectl patch configmap infer-pool -p '{"data":{"prefetch.enabled":"false"}}'`

k8s-bot: deploy rollout started for svc=acme-inc-route -> fallback pool (3 pods); configmap patch applied, 2/3 pods ready.

matt: Routing switched; telemetry shows 503s dropping to near 0 for acme-inc. Sending core and driver logs to S3 now.

deploy-bot: upload complete: s3://redwood-debug/acme/2754321987/core.2145.gz, s3://redwood-debug/acme/2754321987/nvlogs.tgz

ryan: Good. Next steps: 1) analyze core (need gdb + debug symbols) 2) reproduce with mem-probe build to capture allocations 3) evaluate watchdog thresholds to avoid SIGTERM -> kernel reset cascade 4) check yesterday's prefetch heuristic diff for allocation spike.

sara: I'll run the repro script (short curl loop + 4 concurrent requests + long prompt) and attach steps for support call. Repro script: 

```
for i in 1 2 3 4; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n    -d '{"model":"rwd-13b","input":'"'"'$(yes "lorem ipsum" | head -n 200 | tr -d \n)'"'"',"max_tokens":1024}' &
done
wait
```

matt: Copy of the prefetch diff: `git show HEAD~1:eng-runtime/prefetch.cc` indicates we added aggressive prefetch for KV when batch>8. Looks like this pool sees bursty QPS ~12 which triggers prefetch and spikes mem. Rolling that change back is priority.

janet: I've informed acme-inc support: we routed them to a fallback model and are investigating root cause. They asked for ETA — we'll say initial fix/rollback within 2 hours and follow-up with a postmortem.

ryan: I'll own the postmortem. Will include timeline, affected customers, config changes, and a recommended guardrail: kill before prefetch if mem+alloc pattern predicts kernel reset. Also propose auto-fallback to smaller model on repeated OOMs.

matt: OK I'll revert the prefetch patch and deploy canary to one pool. If canary stable for 30m we can rollout.

sara: Found in core backtrace: `libtorch::CUDAAllocator::raw_alloc` shows a large contiguous alloc attempt. That matches prefetch causing a single big allocation instead of incremental.

janet: Support call in 18m, I've got notes. Will update customer that we've applied a short-term route and are rolling back suspected change.

matt: Revert commit applied to canary pool 10:58 UTC. Monitoring.

k8s-bot: canary pods ready (3/3). telemetry: no OOMs on canary in first 5m.

matt: Rolling revert to remaining pools now.

ryan: Marking incident: Sev-2. I'll create incident doc and link artifacts: s3 bucket, logs, core, diffs.

janet: Thanks team. I'll close the customer-facing loop after the postmortem. :white_check_mark:
